correctness.rationale: Exact fractional remainders for the two equal-population pairs reduce all transitions to two parity cases. The two strict intervals are exactly the cases where the small pair total falls; at endpoints a nonlosing tie resolution exists. Because within-pair seats can be nested whenever totals do not fall, the all-tie quantifier is proved. Modular parity enumeration yields the closed counting formula. 39,330 independent exact comparisons and 1,933 period counts corroborate the analytical argument; finite experiments are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two equally sized constituency pairs are a natural symmetry test for Hamilton house monotonicity. The theorem gives an exact all-tie failure classification with a nontrivial house-parity split, the closed count over every rational population period, the unique smallest primitive population witness and first failure at three-to-four seats, and a one-quarter frequency limit for highly unequal pairs. The exact frequency is directly motivated by exposure to house-size changes and is not merely a textbook substitution or an isolated counterexample.
